definition: Keyword for declaring constants in Swift. The initially assigned value can never be changed.
Keyword for declaring variables in Swift. The associated value can be changed at any time during execution.
An environment where multiple processing 'threads' run concurrently. In Swift, carelessness at this level results in so-called Data Races, where state gets corrupted.
A parallel line of execution. Swift now manages this safely under the hood using async/await.
A Swift wrapper that indicates a possible absence of value (nil). Extremely effective at preventing null naturally at compile time.
Swift types indicating that the absence of a value ('nil') is allowed. Safe unwrapping is required from the programmer before access.
Applies an explicit absence marker to a variable. Unlike 'null' in many forms in Java or JavaScript, it requires prior validation before use.
A type focused on value structure ('Value Type'). Any time it is passed around the app, a completely independent and safe copy is created.
A reference-allocation element ('Reference Type'). Multiple parts of the code will share unified instances, consuming resources in common.
Ways of typing and consolidating centralized entities ('Reference Types'). Heavily subject to ARC memory control.
An architecture that segments components. Display rules encapsulated in ViewModels protect the View from managing native data (Models).
Suffix that marks routines running in an asynchronous context. Your main thread stays unblocked while waiting for completion, without choking the app.
Key point where a routine pauses. It warns that further progress depends on the just-started task finishing.
A Reference Type similar to 'Classes', but natively shielded against simultaneous mutations from multiple threads (strictly serial isolation).
Acronym for Automatic Reference Counting. The language's invisible automatic garbage collector, responsible for removing objects from memory only once they have no strong references left.
A modeling flaw in properties where entity A captures B and vice versa, neutralizing cleanup (ARC) and inflating the device's memory indefinitely.
Strict circular (Strong) links between scopes that keep dependencies tied together, blocking RAM cleanup. Often resolved by using 'weak'.
A mitigating indicator when creating references in class scopes; when marked as weak ('weak'), it is omitted from ARC counting, preserving fluidity when deallocation is imminent.
Similar to 'weak' but ignoring optionals. Risky, it relies on an assumption of intrinsic immortality guaranteed during the lifetime of the referenced object.
